title: Bibimbap
subtitle: Korean mixed rice bowl with vegetables, beef, and gochujang
excerpt: The Korean mixed rice bowl: a bowl of warm rice topped with individually seasoned cooked and raw vegetables, marinated beef, a fried egg, and a spoonful of gochujang sauce, all mixed together at the table before eating.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bibimbap (literally mixed rice) is one of the most famous and widely made Korean dishes, with a history that is often traced to ritual food offerings or to the practice of mixing leftover side dishes (banchan) with rice at the end of a meal. The Jeonju and Jinju versions are the most celebrated regional styles. The defining characteristic is that each component is prepared and seasoned separately, then arranged artfully on the rice; the pleasure of the dish is partly visual (the array of colours from the different vegetables) and partly textural (the mixing at the table combines all the separate components and contrasts). The version cooked in a hot stone pot (dolsot bibimbap) adds the element of crunchy rice at the bottom where it has crisped against the stone.

recipeTools.notes: For frying the egg and cooking the vegetables.

content.text: Prepare all the components before assembling: the vegetables are cooked and seasoned separately, then placed in separate portions around the bowl. The egg should be fried sunny-side up so the yolk stays runny and enriches the dish when mixed. Mix the gochujang sauce separately and spoon it on top; let everyone mix their own bowl.

mixed with 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sugar for the sauce

content.text: Marinate the beef: mix with 2 tablespoons of soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of sesame oil, the garlic, and the sugar for at least 15 minutes. Cook in a hot frying pan for 3 to 4 minutes, breaking up any mince, until just cooked and slightly caramelised. Season the blanched spinach and bean sprouts separately with a little sesame oil and soy sauce.

Cook the courgette and carrot matchsticks separately in a little oil over high heat for 1 to 2 minutes each, seasoning with salt. Each vegetable should be cooked briefly, keeping its colour. Make the gochujang sauce by mixing the gochujang with sesame oil, rice vinegar, and sugar.

Divide the warm rice between four bowls. Arrange the beef, vegetables, and a fried egg on top in separate sections around the bowl. Spoon the gochujang sauce on top and scatter with sesame seeds. Serve immediately and mix before eating.
